methodology: The copolypeptoid nanoparticles were prepared through Polypeptoid polymerization-induced self-assembly of N-substituted glycine N-carboxyanhydrides (NNCAs) in dichloromethane (DCM), a solvent with low polarity and weak hydrogen-bonding ability. The polymerization was initiated by isopentylamine, resulting in the formation of spherical or rod-like nano-assemblies at high solid contents.
research_objective: To report the facile preparation of copolypeptoid nanoparticles through Polypeptoid polymerization-induced self-assembly of N-substituted glycine N-carboxyanhydrides (NNCAs) in solvents with low polarity and weak hydrogen-bonding ability, specifically dichloromethane (DCM). The goal was to improve our understanding on NNCA polymerization behaviors and offer an efficient strategy for preparing drug nanocarriers with PSar corona.

key_findings.finding: Polymerization of N-benzyl glycine N-carboxyanhydrides resulted in the formation of spherical or rod-like nano-assemblies within several hours.
The polymerization process was accelerated by using dichloromethane (DCM) as solvent, minimizing side reactions from water and other impurities.
The use of DCM significantly accelerated the polymerization kinetics, leading to well-defined polypeptoids even under open-air conditions.
Synthesis of copolypeptoid nano-assemblies at high solid contents (up to 15%) was completed within several hours in one pot.
Polymerization kinetics was monitored in situ using NMR and FTIR techniques.
GPC experiments were performed on a system equipped with size exclusion columns for polymer characterization.

However, their preparation was limited by the slow polymerization kinetics and low N-substituted glycine N-carboxyanhydride assembly concentrations. Herein, we report the facile preparation of copolypeptoid nanoparticles through Polypeptoid polymerization-induced self-assembly of N-substituted glycine N-carboxyanhydrides (NNCAs) in solvents with Polymerization-induced self-assembly low polarity and weak hydrogen-bonding ability like dichloromethane (DCM). In contrast to the conventional Accelerated polymerization polymerization in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), NNCAs were polymerized at an accelerated rate in DCM that minimized side reactions from water and other impurities. With isopentylamine-initiated PSar as the first sta- bilizing block, the polymerization of N-benzyl glycine N-carboxyanhydrides resulted in the formation of spherical or rod-like nano-assemblies at high solid contents (up to 15%) within several hours. We believe this work not only improves our basic understanding on NNCA polymerization behaviours, but also offers an efficient st no-assemblies at high solid contents (up to 15%) within several hours. We believe this work not only improves our basic understanding on NNCA polymerization behaviours, but also offers an efficient strategy to prepare drug nanocarriers with PSar corona, facilitating the downstream application studies. 1.
